note: Set A covers the wiring schedule rows more completely, including symbol 31 (material, conductor configuration, conduit size) and the conductor-configuration details for symbols 32, 33, 34, 50, 150 and 151, all read correctly against the table. Set B's 14 claims are all accurate and cleanly bound, but it omits the entire symbol 31 row and most conductor-configuration facts, so it drops real engineering content. A's only real flaw is redundancy: symbol 33 and symbol 34 conductor configurations are each stated twice (once with and once without the ground conductors), and the ground conductors are also captured under a separate attribute. Otherwise both sets bind values to the right rows and their quotes support the claims.
remarks: Both sets omit wiring schedule rows 20 (CU: 3#12, #12G., 3/4"C.) and 10 (CU: #12/2WG.); Set B additionally omits row 31 entirely. In Set A the 'conductor configuration' claims that include the ground conductors (e.g. '6#10, 3#10G.', '2#10, #10G.', '3#4/0, #4G.') overlap the separate ground-conductor claims and each other, which is a splitting/deduplication pattern worth normalizing (keep ungrounded conductors in 'conductor configuration' and grounds only in 'ground conductor').
